semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all integers n with n > 1, for all real numbers x, and for all integers m, the equality E_n(x + m) equals E_n(x) holds.

payload.statement_nl: For every integer n>1, every real number x, and every integer m, one has E_n(x + m) = E_n(x).

dependency_self_check.cancellation_check: The integer shift contributes +nm from \lfloor n(x+m)\rfloor and -\sum_{k=1}^n m=-nm from the sum, so the terms cancel exactly.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Fix an integer n>1, a real number x, and an integer m. By definition,

E_n(x+m)=\lfloor n(x+m)\rfloor-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor k(x+m)\rfloor}{k}.

Since nm is an integer, the floor-translation identity gives
\lfloor n(x+m)\rfloor=\lfloor nx+nm\rfloor=\lfloor nx\rfloor+nm.
Likewise, for each integer k with 1\le k\le n, km is an integer, so
\lfloor k(x+m)\rfloor=\lfloor kx+km\rfloor=\lfloor kx\rfloor+km.
Therefore

E_n(x+m)=\bigl(\lfloor nx\rfloor+nm\bigr)-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor kx\rfloor+km}{k}.

Split the sum:

E_n(x+m)=\lfloor nx\rfloor+nm-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor kx\rfloor}{k}-\sum_{k=1}^n m.

Because there are n terms in the last sum, \sum_{k=1}^n m=nm. Hence

E_n(x+m)=\lfloor nx\rfloor-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor kx\rfloor}{k}=E_n(x).

So E_n(x+m)=E_n(x) for all real x and all integers m.
result_payload.proof_summary: Use the floor identity \(\lfloor t+\ell\rfloor=\lfloor t\rfloor+\ell\) for integer \(\ell\), applied to \(t=nx\) and \(t=kx\). The added integer contributions cancel exactly in the definition of \(E_n\), so the function is 1-periodic.

used_external_facts: Standard floor translation identity: \(\lfloor t+\ell\rfloor=\lfloor t\rfloor+\ell\) for integer \(\ell\).
